sections.text: <!-- SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT OR Apache-2.0 -->

Bank reconciliation verifies that every deposit and withdrawal on your bank statement matches your accounting ledger. ERPForAll supports recording or importing bank statements, matching statement lines against open receivable/payable items or counterpart accounts, and posting the resulting bank journal entries cleanly.

* **Bank or Cash Journal**: Configure each company bank account or petty cash box as a journal under **Accounting → More → Configuration → Journals** with its dedicated liquidity account (for example, 101100 Main Bank Account). * **Reconcilable Partner Accounts**: Receivable and payable accounts must have **Allow Reconciliation** enabled so bank lines can settle open invoices or bills directly. * **Accounting Permissions**: Recording statements and reconciling lines requires Accounting user or Accountant permissions.

1. Open **Accounting → More → Accounting → Bank Statements** (or click directly from a Bank journal card on the **Accounting Dashboard**). 2. Click **New** to create a statement manually, or use the statement CSV import option when uploading bank downloads. 3. Fill the statement header: * **Reference**: A clear period or statement identifier (for example, Main Bank Nov 2026). * **Journal**: Select the matching Bank or Cash journal. * **Date**: Statement closing date. * **Starting Balance** and **Ending Balance**: Enter the opening and closing balances from your bank statement to check against **Computed Balance**. 4. Under **Transactions**, click **Add a line** for each bank movement: * Enter **Date**, **Label** (bank description), optional **Partner**, and **Amount** (positive for deposits/receipts, negative for withdrawals/payments). * Optionally assign a **Counterpart Account** (such as bank charges or interest income) or select an open invoice/bill to match. 5. Click **Save** and confirm that **Computed Balance** matches your bank's ending balance. ![A saved Bank Statement displays starting, computed, and ending balances alongside every imported or manually entered transaction line.](/en/next/assets/docs/assets/user-manual/accounting/bank-statement.webp)

1. Open **Accounting → More → Accounting → Bank Reconciliation** to view the **To Reconcile** queue of unmatched statement lines. 2. Select an unreconciled line to inspect its date, label, partner, and amount. 3. Choose how to reconcile the movement: * **Match Open Invoice / Vendor Bill**: Select an unpaid invoice or vendor bill that still has open receivable/payable items to settle it directly. * **Match Counterpart Account**: For bank fees, interest, internal transfers, or expenses without a vendor bill, choose the appropriate **Counterpart Account** (such as *Bank Charges* or an inter-bank suspense/liquidity account). 4. Click **Reconcile** (or **Reconcile All** on the statement header once every line has a valid target). 5. ERPForAll posts the balanced bank journal entry (for example, BNK1/2026/00012), marks the line **RECONCILED**, and updates the statement status automatically. ![A reconciled bank statement line displays the RECONCILED badge and links directly to the generated bank journal entry.](/en/next/assets/docs/assets/user-manual/accounting/bank-reconciled-line.webp)

After completing reconciliation: 1. Return to the **Accounting Dashboard** to verify that the Bank journal card's ledger balance aligns with your latest reconciled statement balance. 2. Open **Accounting → More → Reporting → Cash Flow Statement** or **General Ledger** (filtering on your bank liquidity account) to audit every posted bank journal entry.

* **"No open receivable/payable items left to reconcile"**: This occurs if a statement line points to an invoice or bill that was already paid and reconciled in full via **Register Payment**. Either clear **Match Invoice/Bill** and point the line to the outstanding payments/receipts clearing account (or counterpart liquidity account), or match only invoices with a positive open balance. * **Ending Balance Mismatch**: Check whether any bank line has an inverted sign (withdrawals must be negative, deposits positive) or whether **Starting Balance** differs from the previous statement's closing balance. * **Foreign Currency Bank Lines**: When a bank movement settles a foreign-currency invoice, ERPForAll automatically calculates any realized exchange gain or loss using the company's exchange difference accounts.
<!-- SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT OR Apache-2.0 -->

When your organization operates a holding company and one or more subsidiaries—even across different currencies or local charts of accounts—use **Group Consolidation** inside **Accounting** to produce unified, balanced consolidated financial statements with full audit traceability.

1. Ensure **Group Consolidation** is enabled under **Accounting → More → Configuration → Settings** (see [Controlling, Budgets & Fixed Assets](/en/next/user/accounting-controlling-budgets-assets.md#enable-enterprise-finance)). 2. Verify that all participating subsidiaries are created under **Settings → Users & Companies → Companies** and that your user account has access to the holding and subsidiary companies. 3. Maintain up-to-date closing and average currency exchange rates under **Settings → Reference Data → Currencies** for any foreign-currency subsidiary.

1. Open **Accounting → More → Consolidation → Consolidation Groups** and click **New** (or inspect an existing group). 2. Define the group header: * **Group Name & Code**: Identify the reporting group (for example, Holding Consolidated Group). * **Reporting Currency**: The functional currency in which consolidated statements are presented. 3. On the **Entities** tab, add the parent and each subsidiary with: * **Consolidation Method**: *Full Consolidation* (controlled subsidiaries), *Proportional*, or *Equity Method*. * **Ownership Percentage**: Used automatically to calculate **Non-Controlling Interest (NCI)** when ownership is below 100%. 4. Click **Bootstrap Group FS Chart** to generate a standard group-level financial statement structure (Assets, Liabilities, Equity, Revenue, Expenses, CTA, and NCI lines) and map each entity's local accounts to the corresponding group FS lines.

1. Open **Accounting → More → Consolidation → Consolidation Runs** and click **New**. 2. Select the **Consolidation Group**, target **Period** (start and end dates), and run description (for example, Holding consolidation Jan–Nov 2026). 3. Run the consolidation calculation. ERPForAll executes: * **Currency Translation & CTA**: Translates foreign-subsidiary balance sheet items at closing rate, P&L items at average rate, and historical equity at historical rate, posting the difference automatically to **Cumulative Translation Adjustment (CTA)**. * **Intercompany (IC) Elimination**: Matches and eliminates intercompany receivables/payables, revenues/expenses, and internal balances across group members. * **Non-Controlling Interest (NCI)**: Separates minority share of subsidiary net income and equity based on ownership percentage. * **Automatic Balance Verification**: Confirms **Total Consolidated Assets = Total Consolidated Liabilities & Equity** (Diff $0.00). 4. Review the **Totals**, **Verification**, and **Consolidation Ledger** tabs, then confirm/lock the consolidation run once audited. ![A Consolidation Run summarizes group Assets, Liabilities & Equity, Net Profit, balance verification ($0.00 difference), and consolidation ledger entries.](/en/next/assets/docs/assets/user-manual/accounting/consolidation-run.webp)

Open **Accounting → More → Consolidation** to review group-level outputs: * **Consolidated Balance Sheet**: Presents group financial position after FX translation, IC eliminations, and NCI allocation. * **Consolidated Profit & Loss**: Presents group revenues, expenses, and net profit attributable to parent and non-controlling interests. * **IC Reconciliation Matrix**: Compares paired intercompany balances between every pair of subsidiaries so finance teams can spot and resolve intercompany discrepancies before closing the group period. ![Consolidated Profit & Loss rolls up group revenues, expenses, and net profit across every consolidated entity.](/en/next/assets/docs/assets/user-manual/accounting/consolidated-pnl.webp)

* **Report Shows "No data for these filters"**: Check the **Period** filter at the top of **Consolidated Balance Sheet** or **IC Reconciliation Matrix**—if the default filter is set to **Today**, switch it to **This year** or the exact date range covered by your completed **Consolidation Run**. * **Intercompany Imbalance in IC Matrix**: Open the **IC Reconciliation Matrix**, identify which two entities have an unmatched receivable/payable or revenue/expense pair, verify whether one subsidiary has an unposted draft invoice/bill, post it, and re-run consolidation. * **Unmapped Local Account**: If a subsidiary posts to a newly added local account, map that account to its target **Group FS Chart** line inside the Consolidation Group before re-running the period consolidation.

docs.title: Controlling, Budgets (AVC), and Fixed Assets & CIP

sections.text: <!-- SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT OR Apache-2.0 -->

ERPForAll includes built-in management accounting and asset lifecycle modules directly inside **Accounting**. Enable the enterprise features you need from **Accounting Settings** to unlock Cost & Profit Center Controlling, Real-Time Budget Availability Control (AVC), and Fixed Assets with Construction in Progress (CIP).

1. Open **Accounting → More → Configuration → Settings** (check both **Current company** and **Global settings** scopes as needed). 2. Enable the modules your organization uses: * **Controlling** — *Cost Center & Profit Center Controlling* (unlocks Analytic Plans, Cost & Profit Centers, Default Cost Center Rules, Statistical Key Figures, Cost Allocation Cycles/Runs, and Cost Center Performance). * **Budgeting & AVC** — *Advanced Budgeting & Availability Control (AVC)* (unlocks Budget Control Profiles, Budgets, Budget Amendments, Budget Commitments, and Budget Availability Control report). * **Fixed Assets & CIP** — *Fixed Assets & Construction in Progress (CIP)* (unlocks Asset Classes, Assets & CIP, CIP Settlements, and Depreciation Runs). * **Group Consolidation** — *Group Financial Statement Consolidation* (covered in [Multi-Company Consolidation](/en/next/user/accounting-consolidation.md)). 3. Click **Save** and reload the page so the corresponding menus appear under **Accounting → More**. ![Accounting Settings toggles activate Controlling, Budgeting & AVC, Fixed Assets & CIP, and Group Consolidation.](/en/next/assets/docs/assets/user-manual/accounting/accounting-settings.webp)

1. **Analytic Plans & Cost Centers**: * Configure dimensions under **Accounting → More → Configuration → Analytic Plans** (for example, *Departments* and *Projects*). * Create organizational units under **Configuration → Cost & Profit Centers** (specifying code, center type, parent hierarchy, and analytic plan). * Set **Default Cost Center Rules** so postings to selected accounts or products automatically derive the right cost center. 2. **Statistical Key Figures (SKF) & Cost Allocation Cycles**: * Define allocation drivers (such as headcount, square meters, or server units) under **Configuration → Statistical Key Figures**. * Define overhead distribution rules under **Configuration → Cost Allocation Cycles** (sender cost center, receiver cost centers, SKF driver or fixed percentages). * Execute periodic overhead allocations under **Accounting → More → Accounting → Cost Allocation Runs** and post the allocation entries. 3. **Analytic & Cost Center Reporting**: * Open **Reporting → Analytic Report** or **Reporting → Cost Center Performance** to compare actual costs, revenues, and allocated overhead by cost center and plan. ![Cost & Profit Centers organize internal departments and profit units for management accounting.](/en/next/assets/docs/assets/user-manual/accounting/cost-centers.webp) ![The Analytic Report aggregates posted revenues and expenses across cost centers and analytic plans.](/en/next/assets/docs/assets/user-manual/accounting/analytic-report.webp)

Budget Availability Control monitors commitments (Purchase Orders) and actuals (Vendor Bills / Journal Entries) against approved budgets in real time: 1. **Budget Control Profiles**: Open **Configuration → Budget Control Profiles** to define warning and hard-stop thresholds (for example, *Strict Hard Stop: 80% Warn / 100% Block*). 2. **Create and Activate a Budget**: * Open **Accounting → More → Accounting → Budgets** and click **New**. * Enter the budget name, fiscal period range, and **Budget Control Profile**. * Add budget lines specifying **Account**, **Cost Center**, and **Planned Amount**. * Click **Confirm** and then **Approve & Activate AVC**. Once active, ERPForAll displays **Released**, **Committed**, **Actual**, and **Available** balances on the budget form. 3. **Track Commitments, Amendments, and Utilization**: * Inspect active PO encumbrances under **Accounting → Budget Commitments**. * Request mid-year reallocations or top-ups cleanly under **Accounting → Budget Amendments** so original baseline vs. revised budget remains auditable. * Monitor company-wide utilization percentage under **Reporting → Budget Availability Control**. ![An active AVC Budget tracks Released, Committed, Actual, and Available amounts under your chosen Budget Control Profile.](/en/next/assets/docs/assets/user-manual/accounting/budget-avc.webp)

1. **Asset Classes**: Configure asset categories under **Configuration → Asset Classes** with default fixed asset, accumulated depreciation, and depreciation expense accounts plus method and useful life. 2. **Create a Fixed Asset or CIP Record**: * Open **Accounting → More → Accounting → Assets & CIP** and click **New**. * Enter the asset name, code, **Asset Class**, **Asset Type** (*Fixed Asset* or *Construction in Progress*), acquisition date, acquisition value, depreciation method (*Straight Line* or *Declining Balance*), and number of periods. * Verify the **Fixed Asset / CIP Account**, **Accumulated Depreciation Account**, and **Depreciation Expense Account** fields. 3. **Compute Depreciation & Run Asset**: * Click **Compute Depreciation** to generate the period-by-period **Depreciation Board**. * Confirm/start the asset so its state moves to **Running**. * Post periodic depreciation individually via **Post Next Depreciation** on the asset form or in batch across all running assets under **Accounting → Depreciation Runs**. 4. **Capitalize Construction in Progress (CIP)**: * Accumulate capital project costs on a CIP asset while under construction. * When commissioned, open **Accounting → CIP Settlements** to settle accumulated CIP costs into one or more final depreciable Fixed Assets. ![The Asset Depreciation Board schedules every monthly depreciation entry across the asset's useful life.](/en/next/assets/docs/assets/user-manual/accounting/asset-depreciation-board.webp)

* **Menus Not Visible Under Accounting → More**: Verify the corresponding toggle is enabled in **Accounting Settings** (both Company and Global scopes if multi-company) and reload the browser tab. * **Missing Fixed Asset Account on Save**: If selecting an **Asset Class** does not prefill all three accounting accounts automatically, explicitly choose **Fixed Asset / CIP Account**, **Accumulated Depreciation Account**, and **Depreciation Expense Account** before clicking **Save**. * **AVC Hard-Stop Rejection**: When a Purchase Order or Vendor Bill exceeds 100% of available budget under a Hard Stop profile, either reduce the spend, reallocate funds via a **Budget Amendment**, or have Finance review the Budget Control Profile.

docs.title: Accounting Setup, Chart of Accounts, and Manual Journal Entries

sections.text: <!-- SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT OR Apache-2.0 -->

The **Accounting** application is organized around a journal-based double-entry ledger. Before issuing invoices or closing periods, verify your Chart of Accounts, journals, taxes, payment terms, and fiscal periods so every operational document posts cleanly to the right accounts. ![The Accounting Dashboard groups daily work by journal—Customer Invoices, Vendor Bills, Bank, and Cash—with quick action buttons.](/en/next/assets/docs/assets/user-manual/accounting/dashboard.webp)

Assign accounting roles under **Settings → Users & Companies → Users**: * **Read-only (Accounting Read-Only)**: View posted journal entries, invoices, bills, and financial reports without modifying accounting data. * **Billing / Invoicing User**: Draft and post customer invoices, vendor bills, and payments. * **Accountant / Administrator**: Configure Chart of Accounts, journals, taxes, fiscal positions, fiscal periods, lock dates, controlling, budgets, fixed assets, and group consolidation.

1. Open **Accounting → More → Configuration → Chart of Accounts**. 2. Review existing accounts by **Code**, **Account Name**, **Type** (Asset, Liability, Equity, Income, Expense, Off-Balance), and **Allow Reconciliation**. 3. Enable **Allow Reconciliation** on receivable, payable, and outstanding payment/receipt clearing accounts so payments and credit notes can be matched against open items. 4. Click **New** to add a custom account, assign its code, account type, currency (optional), and any **Account Tags** used for tax or cash-flow classification. ![The Chart of Accounts defines every statutory ledger account, type classification, and reconciliation capability.](/en/next/assets/docs/assets/user-manual/accounting/chart-of-accounts.webp)

Configure daily posting rules under **Accounting → More → Configuration**: * **Journals**: Maintain separate journals for **Sales** (Customer Invoices), **Purchases** (Vendor Bills), **Bank**, **Cash**, and **Miscellaneous** (manual accruals, depreciation, closing entries). Each journal defines its default debit/credit accounts, sequence prefix, and optional dedicated credit-note sequence. * **Taxes & Tax Groups**: Define sales and purchase taxes (percentage or fixed, price-included or price-excluded) together with tax repartition lines and tax accounts. * **Fiscal Positions**: Map default domestic taxes and accounts to export, tax-exempt, or regional equivalents automatically based on the customer or vendor's fiscal position or country. * **Payment Terms**: Configure due-date schedules such as *Immediate Payment*, *15 Days*, *30 Days*, *End of Following Month*, or split installments (for example, 30% upfront and 70% within 30 days).

1. Open **Accounting → More → Configuration → Fiscal Periods** to verify open accounting periods for the current fiscal year. 2. When month-end or year-end review finishes, close or lock completed periods (or set lock dates in **Accounting → More → Configuration → Settings**) to prevent backdated postings from altering audited financial statements. 3. Only authorized Accounting Administrators can adjust lock dates or reopen a closed period if a statutory adjustment is required.

Use manual journal entries for payroll accruals, prepayments, adjustments, or inter-account reclassifications: 1. Open **Accounting → More → Accounting → Journal Entries** and click **New**. 2. Fill the header: **Accounting Date**, **Journal** (typically *Miscellaneous Operations*), **Company**, and a descriptive **Reference** (for example, monthly rent accrual or adjustment memo). 3. Under **Journal Items**, click **Add a line** for each debit and credit leg: * Choose the **Account**, optional **Partner**, **Label**, and **Debit** or **Credit** amount (plus **Analytic Distribution** if Controlling is active). * Confirm that total Debits equal total Credits so the entry is balanced. 4. Click **Save**, review the generated lines, and click **Post**. ERPForAll assigns the final sequence number (such as GEN/2026/11/0003) and locks the entry from direct editing. 5. **Reversing an Entry**: If a posted manual entry needs correction or an accrual must reverse in the next period, click **Reverse Entry**, enter the reversal date and reason, and confirm. ERPForAll posts a linked reversal entry (such as GEN/2026/11/0004) preserving a full audit trail. ![A posted manual journal entry shows balanced debit and credit items, sequence number, and the Reverse Entry action.](/en/next/assets/docs/assets/user-manual/accounting/posted-journal-entry.webp)

* **Entry Will Not Post (Unbalanced)**: Verify that the sum of Debit lines equals the sum of Credit lines to the exact currency precision before clicking **Post**. * **Missing Required Header Fields**: Ensure **Journal**, **Date**, and **Company** are selected before posting a new manual entry. * **Period Locked Error**: If ERPForAll refuses posting on an earlier date, either move the **Accounting Date** to the current open period or ask an Accounting Administrator to review **Fiscal Periods** and lock dates.

docs.title: Customer Invoices, Vendor Bills, Payments, and Credit Notes

sections.text: <!-- SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT OR Apache-2.0 -->

Use the **Customers** and **Vendors** menus in **Accounting** to manage your entire Accounts Receivable (AR) and Accounts Payable (AP) lifecycle—from drafting and posting documents to partial settlements, full payments, credit notes, batch payments, and overdue follow-ups.

Verify the following before recording AR/AP documents: * **Active Company & Journals**: Confirm the active company in the top-right header and ensure active Sales, Purchase, and Bank/Cash journals exist. * **Partner Master Data**: Confirm that the customer or vendor has accurate billing address, tax ID, and default payment terms. * **User Access**: Creating, posting, and paying invoices or bills requires Accounting user permissions.

1. Navigate to **Accounting → Customers → Invoices** and click **New**. 2. Select the **Customer**, confirm **Invoice Date**, **Payment Terms** (or explicit **Due Date**), **Journal**, and **Currency**. 3. Under **Invoice Lines**, click **Add a line** to select the **Product** (or enter a description), **Quantity**, **Unit Price**, optional **Discount (%)**, and **Taxes** (for example, VAT 11% (Sales)). 4. Click **Save** and review **Untaxed Amount**, **Tax**, and **Total**. 5. Click **Confirm** (or **Post**). ERPForAll assigns the official invoice number (for example, INV/2026/00025), posts the receivable and revenue/tax journal items, and displays **Register Payment** and **Credit Note**. ![A posted Customer Invoice shows the assigned number, tax breakdown, total due, and Register Payment and Credit Note actions.](/en/next/assets/docs/assets/user-manual/accounting/customer-invoice-posted.webp)

You can settle an invoice or vendor bill in one payment or across multiple installments: 1. Open the posted invoice or vendor bill and click **Register Payment**. 2. Choose the **Journal** (such as *Main Bank* or *Petty Cash Box*), **Payment Method**, **Payment Date**, and **Amount**: * **Partial Payment**: Enter an amount lower than the open balance (for example, $100.00 against $333.00). ERPForAll displays the **Payment Difference** ($233.00) and defaults to **Keep open** so the remaining balance stays collectible. * **Write-Off Difference**: If the difference is a bank fee, rounding, or agreed early-payment discount, choose **Mark as fully paid** and select the write-off account and label. 3. Click **Create Payment**. 4. For a partial payment, the invoice displays its reduced **Amount Due** and links the payment in the **Payments** smart button. Repeat **Register Payment** for the remaining balance to reconcile the invoice to **PAID** with $0.00 Amount Due. ![The Register Payment dialog calculates partial payment differences automatically and lets you keep the balance open or write it off.](/en/next/assets/docs/assets/user-manual/accounting/register-payment-partial.webp) ![Once settled in full, the invoice displays the PAID badge, zero Amount Due, and a Payments smart button linking every payment entry.](/en/next/assets/docs/assets/user-manual/accounting/customer-invoice-paid.webp)

When a customer returns goods, cancels a service, or receives a price adjustment on a posted invoice: 1. Open the posted Customer Invoice and click **Credit Note** (or open **Accounting → Customers → Credit Notes → New**). 2. In the **Credit Note** wizard, select the **Credit Method** (partial refund draft or full reversal), enter a clear **Reason** and **Reversal Date**, and confirm. 3. Review the generated Credit Note (numbered RINV/...), adjust line quantities if issuing a partial refund, and click **Confirm** to post the reversal to the ledger. 4. For vendor refunds, follow the same steps from a posted Vendor Bill (or open **Accounting → Vendors → Refunds**). ![A posted Credit Note reverses the targeted invoice lines and maintains a direct reference to the original invoice.](/en/next/assets/docs/assets/user-manual/accounting/credit-note-posted.webp)

1. Navigate to **Accounting → Vendors → Bills** and click **New** (or create a draft bill directly from a confirmed Purchase Order—see [Purchasing and Receipts](/en/next/user/buy-and-receive.md)). 2. Select the **Vendor**, enter the **Bill Date** and vendor invoice **Reference**, and verify the **Journal** and **Accounting Date**. 3. Add expense or inventory lines under **Invoice Lines**, verify purchase taxes and total, click **Save**, and click **Confirm** to post (assigning a sequence such as BILL/2026/11/0021). 4. Click **Register Payment** when paying the vendor to post the outgoing payment and update the bill status to **PAID**. ![A posted Vendor Bill records the payable liability and exposes Register Payment and vendor refund actions.](/en/next/assets/docs/assets/user-manual/accounting/vendor-bill-posted.webp)

* **Batch Payments** (**Customers → Batch Payments** / **Vendors → Batch Payments**): Group multiple individual payments from the same journal into one deposit slip or bank payment batch so a single bank statement line can reconcile multiple invoices or bills. * **Follow-up Reports** (**Customers → Follow-up Reports**): Review overdue customer receivables grouped by configured **Follow-up Levels** (**Configuration → Follow-up Levels**) so finance teams can track reminders and overdue balances systematically. * **Recurring & Deferred Entries** (**Accounting → More → Accounting → Recurring & Deferred**): Automate periodic revenue recognition, prepaid expense amortization, or recurring monthly journal schedules.

* **Missing Bill Date**: Vendor bills require an explicit **Bill Date** before posting (especially when generated from a Purchase Order). Fill **Bill Date** on the form header before clicking **Confirm**. * **Reopening or Fixing a Posted Document**: Posted invoices and bills are immutable for audit integrity. Use **Credit Note** / **Refund** to reverse mistakes rather than deleting posted documents. * **Invoice Still Open After Payment**: Confirm that the payment was posted to a reconcilable receivable/payable partner account and open the **Payments** smart button to verify reconciliation.
